summary: This is a tutorial from the SDFormat documentation (version 1.6 of the page) explaining the Gazebo extension to URDF, the <gazebo> tag, which lets URDF users add SDFormat-specific elements that are carried into the converted SDFormat output. It covers how <gazebo> tags without a reference apply to the robot model, how reference-based tags modify links and joints via special tags (e.g., mu1, kp, selfCollide, springStiffness, preserveFixedJoint), and how fixed joint lumping merges a fixed child link into its parent by default and how to disable it. The page is example-heavy, showing URDF inputs and resulting SDFormat outputs.
one_line: Tutorial on the SDFormat <gazebo> extension to URDF, covering link and joint special tags and fixed joint lumping.
key_facts: When URDF files are loaded by Gazebo, the URDF content is first converted to SDFormat before being processed by Gazebo.
The command gz sdf -p <path to urdf file> can be used to convert a URDF file to SDFormat for inspection.
A <gazebo> tag without a reference attribute applies to the SDFormat <model> generated from the <robot> URDF tag.
For links, the mu1 tag maps to collision/surface/friction/ode/mu in the SDFormat output.
The dampingFactor link tag multiplies the previous link velocity by (1-dampingFactor) and maps to velocity_decay/linear and velocity_decay/angular.
The selfCollide tag, when true, allows the link to collide with other links in the model and maps to self_collide.
The laserRetro tag sets the intensity value returned by a laser sensor and maps to collision/laser_retro.
For joints, springStiffness is in N/m and maps to axis/dynamics/spring_stiffness; springReference maps to axis/dynamics/spring_reference.
The fudgeFactor joint tag scales the excess for a joint motor at joint limits and should be between zero and one.
Fixed joint lumping is enabled by default and merges the child link's visual and collision elements into the parent link, discarding the fixed joint.
As of libsdformat 9.9.0, frame elements representing the discarded joint and child link are generated to preserve their pose information.
Setting preserveFixedJoint to true results in a joint with a fixed type, whereas disableFixedJointLumping to true results in a revolute joint with position limits set to 0.
If both preserveFixedJoint and disableFixedJointLumping are true, preserveFixedJoint takes precedence.
Fixed joint lumping can be disabled for all joints by setting ParserConfig::URDFPreserveFixedJoint to true.
Disabling joint lumping should only be done when both parent and child links have positive mass and corresponding <inertial> elements.
The <material> tag directly under <gazebo> accepts Gazebo-classic material script names such as Gazebo/SkyBlue or Gazebo/WoodFloor; it is only relevant for Gazebo-classic.
At the time of writing, a bug in the URDF to SDFormat converter (sdformat issue 333) behaves incorrectly when visual and collision tags in the URDF have names.
